values.DataCenterNotes: The Wisconsin commission case page for the Rochester Lateral says the pipeline will give firm gas to the proposed Oak Creek combustion turbine plant and the Paris engine plant, and later to the Elm Road station. A Milwaukee public radio report on the May 2025 commission approval of the Oak Creek and Paris plants says We Energies cited growing demand, including an incoming Microsoft data center in Racine County. A University of Wisconsin extension article gives the same link.

verifications.note: Case page for the Rochester Lateral. States the need is firm gas for the Oak Creek Combustion Turbine, the Paris engine plant, and later the Elm Road station.
Says the commission approved the Oak Creek and Paris plants and We Energies points to a Microsoft data center being built in Racine County as a reason.
Page loaded and mentions data centers in connection with the approved plants.

records.researcher_notes: The Rochester Lateral supplies the new Oak Creek gas turbine plant and the Paris engine plant. We Energies and the state commission tied those plants to the Microsoft data center in Mount Pleasant. The commission page and the radio report are different publishers.

ledger.note: Searched the lateral extension with data center. Sources describe only a 10 mile lateral for the Texas LNG export plant in Brownsville. No data center tie found.

The Lakeshore Lateral runs about 46 miles from Bluff Creek to near Interstate 94 in the Town of Paris. The state agriculture department filing and news coverage call it a capacity addition for southeast Wisconsin and name no power plant. The sister Rochester Lateral case page is the one that names the Oak Creek and Paris plants. No We Energies or commission source found that ties Lakeshore to a plant or to data center load, so it stays blank.
Serves the Oak Creek combustion turbine and Paris engine plants. We Energies and the commission tied those plants to the Microsoft Mount Pleasant data center.
